title: How Much Does It Cost to Launch a D2C Brand in India in 2026? A Month-by-Month Breakdown
summary: Starting a direct-to-consumer brand in India in 2026 costs between ₹45,000 and ₹6 lakh for the first 90 days, depending on your validation stage, product
body_markdown:
Starting a direct-to-consumer brand in India in 2026 costs between ₹45,000 and ₹6 lakh for the first 90 days, depending on your validation stage, product category, and city tier. You have read three starter budget guides this week. One says ₹50,000. One says ₹3.5 lakh. One says ₹10 lakh. None tells you which number applies to your situation.


The real fear is not the launch number. It is Month 2: inventory paid for, ads running, repeat orders not yet arriving.


Published ranges vary wildly for three mechanical reasons. Most bundle agency build fees into “starter cost.” Many leave out the two line items that decide whether you survive Month 3: RTO losses and payment costs. Several quote statutory fees that are zero at the government level.


This guide gives you one itemized, 2026-dated, month-by-month cost build-up across three realistic tiers, with sourced figures where they exist and labelled estimates where they do not.


Context worth holding: the India D2C e-commerce market was valued at USD 87.5 billion in 2025 and is estimated to reach USD 322.1 billion by 2031 (Mordor Intelligence, 2026).


### Key Takeaways


- **Three realistic Months 1-3 tiers:** Bootstrap at roughly ₹45,000-₹95,000, Lean Launch at ₹1.2-2.5 lakh, Proper Launch at ₹3-6 lakh.
- **[Razorpay’s 90-day welcome offer](https://razorpay.com/pricing/) waives the standard 2% platform fee** entirely on domestic transactions up to Rs 5 lakh cumulative GMV for new merchants, meaning your payment processing cost in Months 1-3 can be effectively zero on your first few hundred orders, leaving that budget for inventory and ad testing where pre-validation brands need it most.
- **Five cost buckets:** compliance, store and checkout, inventory and packaging, shipping and RTO, marketing.
- **The highest hidden cost is RTO** , at ₹150-300 per order, against an India RTO rate of 25-35%.
- **Two 2026 changes most budgets miss:** the GST 2.0 slab restructure and the UPI MDR framework from 15 October 2026.
- **The number founders get wrong:** they budget registration too high and RTO at zero.


## How much does it actually cost to launch a D2C brand in India in Months 1-3?


A realistic Months 1-3 outlay falls into three tiers. Bootstrap runs roughly ₹45,000-₹95,000, Lean Launch ₹1.2-2.5 lakh, and Proper Launch ₹3-6 lakh. Each covers registration, store and checkout, first inventory, packaging, shipping, an RTO buffer, and initial ad spend across the full 90 days, not just launch week.


These tiers are not good, better, best. They map to validation stage, not ambition.

### Why the ranges you’ve seen online vary so wildly


- Most estimates bundle agency build fees into “starter cost,” inflating the baseline before you spend a rupee on product.
- Many omit RTO and payment costs, which makes Month 3 look cheaper than it is.
- Several quote registration costs that are zero at the government level.


**DID YOU KNOW:** Incorporating a private limited company still carries a government filing fee, because MCA SPICe+ filing fees are not zero for authorised capital up to ₹15 lakh; registration fees are calculated based on the slab-based structure defined in the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules (MCA, Schedule XI).


### GST: Is it mandatory on day one, or can it wait?


Registration becomes mandatory at ₹40 lakh turnover for goods and ₹20 lakh for services in most states, with lower limits for special category states. Check your state’s GST registration limits before assuming exemption.


Composition scheme caps range from ₹50 lakh to ₹1.5 crore depending on state and supplier type, check eligibility before assuming you qualify.


The practical trigger is not turnover. Selling through marketplaces or making inter-state taxable supplies requires registration regardless of turnover. Registering early also lets you claim input tax credit on setup costs.


## Which payment gateway works for a D2C startup in India, and what does it cost?


For a D2C startup, the payment gateway needs to activate for free, collect payments without a website, settle funds fast enough to reorder inventory, and reduce RTO on COD orders. Razorpay covers all four: free activation, Payment Links for no-website sellers, instant settlements 24/7/365, and Magic Checkout for RTO reduction, at 2% plus GST with no monthly minimum.


Razorpay’s Payment Gateway processes domestic transactions at a 90 to 95 percent success rate, against an industry average of 85 to 88 percent. For a founder doing 100 orders in Month 1, that gap means roughly 7 to 10 fewer failed transactions, each of which is a customer you would have to re-acquire.


That matters at low volume. A founder doing 40 orders in Month 1 pays on 40 orders, not against a slab they never reach. When you[integrate a payment gateway](https://razorpay.com/blog/how-to-integrate-payment-gateway-in-website) , the technical work is the cost, not the activation.


Settlement timing decides whether Month 2 reorders are funded. Razorpay[instant settlements](https://razorpay.com/blog/instant-settlement-payment-gateway) give 24/7/365 access to funds within seconds, against a standard T+2 cycle.


**PRO-TIP:** New merchants may be eligible for limited-period platform fee waivers during their first 90 days, subject to GMV caps and payment-method exclusions. Check current eligibility terms rather than assuming standard rates apply from day one.

## What hidden costs will blow up your starter budget if you ignore them?


Return-to-Origin is the single largest hidden cost in an Indian D2C starter budget. It costs sellers ₹150-300 per order (Shiprocket Logistics Report, 2025), and India’s average RTO rate runs 25-35% against a global benchmark of 8-12% (IBEF E-commerce Report, 2026). A founder who budgets RTO at zero will see real margins land well below the spreadsheet. For scale: a 20% RTO rate can wipe out 4-6% of net margin.


There is a second cash killer nobody itemizes. Most logistics aggregators settle COD in D+3 to D+7, and direct courier arrangements can take D+7 to D+14 (Delhivery, Ecom Express standard terms), leaving a seller with 500 COD orders at ₹800 AOV holding roughly ₹2.80 lakh in transit. Instant settlement products — available from most major payment gateways, let you access prepaid order funds within hours instead of waiting for T+2, which can fund Month 2 reorders from Month 1 revenue.


### Prepaid vs COD: the rupee gap that changes your pricing


Industry data shows about 26% RTO on COD or non-prepaid orders, against under 2% for prepaid. On 100 COD orders, that is roughly 26 returns at ₹150-300 each, or ₹3,900 to ₹7,800 gone. On 100 prepaid orders, it is under ₹600.


**PRO-TIP:** A ₹50 prepaid incentive is almost always cheaper than absorbing the return leg. Given ₹150-300 per RTO order and the 26% COD versus under-2% prepaid gap, price the prepaid discount in from day one.


Brands report meaningful gains from doing this deliberately: a 42-48% decrease in return rates, 89% retention of COD conversion volumes, and ₹3.2-4.1 improvement in contribution margin per order within 90-120 days. Just do not switch off[cash on delivery](https://razorpay.com/blog/cash-on-delivery/) entirely, because first-time buyers still lean on it.


### Will the October 2026 UPI MDR change affect your payment costs?


From 15 October 2026, merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000 are scheduled to attract an MDR of 0.4%, capped at Rs 300, borne by the merchant.


The exemptions are wide. Person-to-person transfers, payments up to Rs 2,000, and eligible small merchants remain outside the framework, and consumers do not pay MDR directly. NPCI has stated that small merchants and 96% of transactions remain unaffected.


Practical implication: any starter kit priced above ₹2,000 carries an MDR cost that a ₹1,999 SKU does not.

## How should you price your product to survive Months 1-3, not just launch?


Your launch MRP has to fund three things at once: GST liability, acquisition cost, and an RTO buffer. It also has to remain viable for a second purchase, because a 90-day repeat rate below 20% means you are running paid traffic to a leaky bucket.


### Working out MRP after GST 2.0


Rates have been simplified into two main slabs of 5% and 18%, removing 12% and 28%, with sin and luxury goods at 40%. The[ratio](https://busy.in/gst/gst-slabs-5-percent-18-percent/) nalisation took effect on 22 September 2025, with 99% of items in the old 12% slab moving to 5%. MRP models built on pre-2025 slab assumptions will be wrong. Recheck your category slab before you print labels.


### Pricing differently for your own store versus marketplaces


Marketplace TCS was halved to 0.5% with effect from 10 July 2024 under Notification No. 15/2024-Central Tax, and it is creditable against output tax liability once the operator files, so treat it as a timing cost. Even so, after commissions and fulfilment differences, your own-store price and marketplace price cannot be the same number.


### Build a CAC-inflation buffer into your floor price


**PRO-TIP:** India remains one of the cheapest large ad markets, with Facebook CPM at $1.36 in India against $16.08 in the United States. But Meta CPM rose 20.03% year over year in 2025 on a global, aggregate ecommerce benchmark rather than an India-specific one. Build a buffer for a 20% rise in[customer acquisition cost](https://razorpay.com/learn/customer-acquisition-cost/) before you lock an MRP.


Category growth is strong, with Health and Pharma up 48%, BPC 41%, and Fashion 21%, but that only compounds if the second order is economically attractive.


## Bootstrap vs Lean vs Proper: which starter budget tier is right for you?


Choose Bootstrap only to validate raw demand with under 100 orders. Move to Lean Launch once you have usable product photos and one proven ad angle. Spend at Proper Launch level only after you have validated repeat purchase intent.


### Decision checklist: match your validation stage to your budget tier


Where you are right now Tier What you are buying

Measurable 90-day repeat above 20% Proper Launch Scale on proven economics


The gate between Lean and Proper is not revenue. It is retention. A sub-20% 90-day repeat rate means more spend buys more leakage.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### **Do I need GST registration before my first sale?**


Not always. Thresholds are ₹40 lakh for goods and ₹20 lakh for services in most states. But selling through marketplaces or making inter-state taxable supplies triggers mandatory registration regardless of turnover. Many founders register early to claim input tax credit on setup and inventory costs.


### Does Razorpay offer free payment processing for new D2C brands?


Yes. Razorpay’s 90-day welcome offer waives the standard 2% platform fee on domestic Payment Gateway transactions for new merchants, up to Rs 5,00,000 in cumulative GMV. Credits are applied automatically when you complete KYC and activate your account on or after 1 July 2026; no promo code needed. GST, statutory levies, and the Rs 199 KYC processing fee are not waived. The offer is limited to one redemption per PAN or bank account, and excludes prepaid cards, corporate credit cards, American Express, Diners Club, and all EMI-based payment methods. Unused credits lapse after 90 days.


### Are UPI payments still free for merchants in India?


Not entirely, from October 2026. Starting 15 October 2026, merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000 attract an MDR of 0.4%, capped at Rs 300, borne by the merchant. Payments up to Rs 2,000, person-to-person transfers, and eligible small merchants remain exempt. NPCI has stated that 96% of transactions remain unaffected.


### **How much should I set aside specifically for RTO in my first 90 days?**


Use this method: expected orders x expected COD share x India’s 25-35% RTO rate x ₹150-300 per RTO order. For 300 orders at 60% COD and a 28% RTO rate, that is roughly 50 returns, or ₹7,500 to ₹15,000.


### **Is it cheaper to register as a sole proprietor or a Private Limited company?**


Proprietorship is cheaper, but the gap is smaller than founders expect. MCA SPICe+ filing fees are not zero up to ₹15 lakh authorised capital; they follow the slabs in the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, with a typical total one-time outlay of ₹8,000-₹18,000. The real difference is professional fees and ongoing compliance effort.


### **Does my product category change my starter budget significantly?**


Yes. Food brands carry FSSAI at ₹100 to ₹7,500 depending on licence class. Category growth also differs sharply, with Health and Pharma at 48%, BPC at 41%, and Fashion at 21%, which changes how fast ad spend recovers.


### **Is a payment gateway free to set up in India?**


Yes. Razorpay’s Payment Gateway is free to activate and charges only on successful transactions, at a standard domestic rate of 2% plus applicable GST. A one-time Rs 199 KYC processing fee plus applicable taxes applies. There is no monthly minimum.
